title: Numerals 2: 2, 3, 4 Take the Genitive Singular
description: After 2, 3, and 4 (and оба/обе), the noun goes into the genitive singular: две книги, три брата, четыре окна. Два/две splits by gender.
descriptionRussian: После 2, 3, 4 (а также оба/обе) существительное стоит в родительном падеже единственного числа: две книги, три брата, четыре окна. «Два» и «две» различаются по роду.
intro: The small-number rule from A1, now with the endings spelled out and one addition. The word for 'both' behaves exactly like the number two, gender split included, which is worth knowing because it turns up constantly and looks nothing like a number. The velar spelling rule fires inside these forms too, so the feminine ending is not always the one you expect.
rules: After 2, 3, and 4 the noun goes into the GENITIVE SINGULAR: две книги, три брата, четыре окна. It looks plural in English but is grammatically genitive singular.
The genitive singular endings are the ones you already know: masculine брат -> брата, feminine книга -> книги, neuter окно -> окна.
Only the number 2 splits by gender: два for masculine/neuter (два стола, два окна), две for feminine (две книги). Три and четыре never change for gender.
Watch the spelling rule after к/г/х: книга -> две книги (-и, never -ы); рука -> две руки.
Оба (masculine/neuter) and обе (feminine), meaning 'both', also take the genitive singular and split by gender: оба брата, обе сестры.
examples: У меня две книги. (I have two books.) feminine две + genitive singular книги.
В классе три брата. (There are three brothers in the class.) три + genitive singular брата.
В комнате четыре окна. (There are four windows in the room.) четыре + genitive singular окна.
На столе два стакана. (There are two glasses on the table.) masculine два + genitive singular стакана.
Я купил два билета. (I bought two tickets.) masculine два + genitive singular билета.
Обе сестры приехали. (Both sisters arrived.) feminine обе + genitive singular сестры.

items.hint: After 2 the noun is genitive singular. The genitive singular of книга is...?
items.explanation: After 2, 3, 4 the noun takes the genitive singular. Книга -> книги (note the spelling rule: -и after к, not -ы). Книг would be the genitive plural, used only after 5 and up.

items.promptEnglish: There are three brothers in the family.
items.hint: Three takes the genitive singular. The genitive singular of брат is брата.
items.explanation: After 3 the noun is genitive singular: брат -> брата. Братьев is the genitive plural (used after 5 and up: пять братьев), and брат alone is the nominative.

items.promptEnglish: There are four windows on the wall.
items.explanation: Четыре is the plain number 'four', which takes the genitive singular окна. Четырёх is its non-nominative form (used in phrases like 'из четырёх'), and четвёртый means 'fourth' (an ordinal).

items.hint: Билет is masculine. Which form of 'two' is masculine?
items.explanation: Билет is masculine, so 'two' is два, not две. Only the number 2 splits by gender: два (masculine/neuter), две (feminine). The noun stays genitive singular: билета.

items.promptEnglish: There are two beds in the room.
items.hint: Кровать is feminine. Which form of 'two' is feminine?
items.explanation: Кровать is feminine, so 'two' is две: две кровати. Два would be wrong here (masculine/neuter). The noun is genitive singular: кровать -> кровати.

items.hint: Сестра is feminine. 'Both' splits by gender just like два/две.
items.explanation: Сестра is feminine, so 'both' is обе (оба is masculine/neuter). Like два/две, обе takes the genitive singular: обе сестры.

blanks: Я был там три _____. (I was there three weeks.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: After 3 the noun is genitive singular: неделя -> недели. Недель is the genitive plural (used after 5: пять недель), and неделю would be the accusative singular.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are two glasses on the table.
errorCorrection.explanation: After 2, 3, and 4 the noun goes into the genitive singular: два стакана. Стакан is the bare nominative, correct after один (один стакан) but not after два. Стаканов is the genitive plural, which belongs after 5 and up (пять стаканов). From два through четыре, always reach for the genitive singular.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Both windows in the room are open.
errorCorrection.explanation: Оба / обе splits by gender exactly like два / две: оба for masculine and neuter, обе for feminine. Окно is neuter, so the form is оба: оба окна. Обе would be right for feminine nouns (обе сестры). Обо is a preposition variant, not a numeral.

Оба ('both') splits by gender just like два/две: оба for masculine and neuter, обе for feminine. Билет is masculine, so the form is оба: оба билета, with the noun in the genitive singular. Обе is the feminine form (обе сестры). Обоих and обеих are the non-nominative forms used once the phrase leaves the nominative (с обоими друзьями, у обеих сестёр). Билет is inanimate, so its accusative matches the nominative, and оба билета is the form to use.

minimalPairs.explanation: After 2 the noun is genitive SINGULAR: книги. Книг is the genitive PLURAL, which belongs after 5 and up (пять книг). This is the core 2-4 vs 5+ split: 2, 3, 4 take the singular form, 5 and up take the plural form.
Билет is masculine, so 'two' is два, not две. The form две is for feminine nouns only (две книги). The number 2 is the only number that splits by gender; три and четыре never do.

reviewVocab.definition: the number 2 takes the genitive singular; два for masculine/neuter, две for feminine. Only 2 splits by gender.
reviewVocab.example: Два стола, два окна, две книги.

reviewVocab.definition: 3 and 4 also take the genitive singular and do NOT change for gender.
reviewVocab.example: Три брата, четыре окна, три сестры.

reviewVocab.definition: 'both'; оба for masculine/neuter, обе for feminine. Takes the genitive singular like два/две.
reviewVocab.example: Оба брата приехали. Обе сестры здесь.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each phrase by whether 'two' should be два or две.
